thread:
incident-bot: ALERT: Dedicated pool kairos-prod-42 (tenant: kairos-corp) GPU utilization 95% · queue length ↑ · 502s retry spike. Paging oncall alex. links: https://redwood.mon/alerts/4977778888 :rotating_light:

alex (oncall): Got the page, looking now. Can someone share quick metrics?

prod-alerts-bot: recent metrics snapshot: avg latency 420ms -> 1.9s  (1m/5m), queue depth 128 -> 640, token-rate per GPU dropped 48% since 12:34 UTC.

sara (sre): Seeing queued tasks piling. This is single-tenant dedicated pool for Kairos — no other tenants to evict. Likely sustained load spike from their nightly job.

mike (eng): Confirmed an uptick in request rate from kairos-corp, 4x baseline. Their model runs long sequences and isn't benefiting from prefix cache.

alex (oncall): Runbook options: 1) emergency burst (reserved burst capacity) 2) trigger emergency autoscale (if allowed for this pool) 3) throttle/soft-fail customer (undesirable). What's Kairos ok with?

kairos-support: Kairos on call (Lydia) is on the thread privately. They confirm an internal batch kicked off accidentally. They request a short burst to clear backlog, then throttle their job.

ops-runbook-bot: Runbook: Dedicated Pool Saturation -> recommended: attempt manual burst up to 60m if customer approves. Command: `redwoodctl pools burst --pool kairos-prod-42 --minutes 60 --reason "customer-approved-burst"`

sara (sre): Two checks before burst: verify available burst quota, and ensure no cross-region dependency. I'll check quota.

mike (eng): I'll warm a spare host image and prepare scaleup plan. If burst fails, fallback is to reduce concurrency via `redwoodctl tenant update --tenant kairos-corp --max-concurrency 8` (soft limit).

alex (oncall): Sara, status?

sara (sre): Burst quota available 1x full rack. No cross-region conflicts. I recommend approving a 60m burst.

kairos-support: Kairos (Lydia): We approve one-time burst for 60 minutes. We'll suppress their batch in 10m.

alex (oncall): Action: performing manual burst now. Executing: `redwoodctl pools burst --pool kairos-prod-42 --minutes 60 --reason "kairos-surge-2026-03-17"`

alex (oncall): Command returned 202 Accepted. Provisioning 8 GPUs (2 nodes). ETA ~90s.

prod-alerts-bot: NOTE: new nodes provisioning. Pool capacity +200% pending.

mike (eng): Warmed images attached, routing policy updated. Watching queue drain.

(some logs):
alex (oncall): `2026-03-17T12:38:12Z pool kairos-prod-42: added nodes n-78,n-79`
sara (sre): `queue depth 640 -> 220 @12:40`

kairos-support: Lydia: Our batch ended early — toggled internal flag. Thanks, pulling back load.

alex (oncall): Queue continues to drain. Latency returning to baseline 500ms.

ops-runbook-bot: Runbook step: monitor for 15m after stabilization then release burst if safe.

mike (eng): Agree. I'll keep autoscale enabled for the window and add green check when stable.

sara (sre): After 20m stable, schedule manual burst release. Plan: `redwoodctl pools release-burst --pool kairos-prod-42 --reason "stabilized"`

alex (oncall): Notifying account team and customer success. Filing incident ticket INC-2026-245 for follow-up and billing note for burst usage.

kairos-support: Lydia: Appreciate the fast response. We'll follow up with our infra team to prevent recurrences.

mike (eng): Quick follow-ups for postmortem: - root cause: accidental internal job; - mitigation: temporary burst accepted - action items: add client-side rate limiter, improve alerts to detect batch-type jobs earlier, consider per-tenant pre-burst guardrail (auto-notify customer before auto-burst).

alex (oncall): Handoff: I'm oncall until 13:00 UTC. Mike will take post-incident review. If anything regresses reopen thread.

incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: pool kairos-prod-42 stabilized. Summary: 60m manual burst used for 18m; queue cleared; no customer-visible errors beyond increased latency during window. Follow-up: INC-2026-245 created. :white_check_mark:
